advice: Abstain. The supplied evidence does not establish a distinct, useful legal loop order for the seven-product Strassen path. The measured three-buffer candidate already uses immediate signed recombination and loses all ten paired controls; changing only product order has no supported basis for addressing that regression. risks: Advice is unverified, not a measured fact. Any future loop-order change must still compute all seven products and fully overwrite all 512×512 outputs, preserve the gemm ABI and full k reductions, and keep packing, allocation, recombination, and cleanup timed. Check FP32 tolerance 0.002, finite output, input immutability, output guards, cancellation and scale-sensitive cases, plus fallback sizes, tails, n<=0, and allocation failure before paired timing.
